chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Musa ibn Bakr, from 'Abd Salih عليه السلام:

Concerning a man who struck another man with a stick and did not lift the stick until he died, he said: “He is to be handed over to the heirs of the slain, but he is not to be left so that they take pleasure in tormenting him; rather, the sentence is to be carried out against him with the sword.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ: the heirs or legal guardians of the slain person who hold the right of retaliation
key_terms.بِالسَّيْفِ: with the sword, indicating swift and regulated execution of retaliation
key_terms.بِعَصًا: with a stick, specifying the instrument of assault
key_terms.ضَرَبَ: struck or beat, indicating the violent act committed
key_terms.مَاتَ: died, indicating the fatal outcome of the assault
key_terms.يَتَلَذَّذُ بِهِ: take pleasure in tormenting him, meaning inflicting gratuitous suffering is forbidden

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man beats another with a stick until he dies?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning intentional killing by prolonged beating with a stick. It states that the killer is subject to retaliation through the authority of the slain person's heirs, but the execution of retaliation must be regulated and not turned into torture.
